title: Trump Picks Bill Pulte as Acting DNI — No Intelligence Background; Replaces Tulsi Gabbard
detail: On June 2, 2026 (Day 499), President Trump named Bill Pulte — currently serving as head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA), overseeing Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac — as acting Director of National Intelligence, replacing Tulsi Gabbard who announced her resignation effective June 30, 2026. Pulte, a real estate investor and social media philanthropist known for giving away money on X (formerly Twitter), has no intelligence community background. He will hold both his FHFA role and the acting DNI position simultaneously. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer immediately condemned the appointment, calling Pulte 'a partisan thug with no experience in intelligence.' The pick raised concerns among intelligence professionals and Democrats about politicization of the intelligence community at a time when the US-Iran war (Day 94) is ongoing and ceasefire negotiations are in crisis.

media.caption: Trump names FHFA chief Bill Pulte as acting Director of National Intelligence, replacing Tulsi Gabbard

title: Iran Formally Suspends Ceasefire Negotiations (Day 94); IRGC Quds Force Chief Warns Bab el-Mandeb Could Become Like Hormuz
detail: On June 2, 2026 — Day 94 of the US-Iran war — Iran formally announced the suspension of all negotiations and message exchanges with the United States via intermediaries. Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi stated that the ceasefire 'is unequivocally a ceasefire on all fronts, including in Lebanon,' and that Israel's escalating offensive in southern Lebanon's suburbs constituted a violation of the ceasefire framework — nullifying the broader truce. IRGC Quds Force commander Brigadier General Esmail Qa'ani separately warned that the Bab al-Mandab Strait — the strategic chokepoint between Yemen and Djibouti through which approximately 4.7 million barrels of oil transit daily — would face the same traffic restrictions as the Strait of Hormuz if Israel continued operations in Lebanon and Gaza. Iran also threatened seizure of Bahraini and Emirati territory if the US 'makes any mistakes.' In response, Trump posted on Truth Social that talks were continuing at a 'rapid pace,' then told CNBC the talks 'started to get very boring' and he didn't care if they ended. Trump told ABC News he believed a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz was reachable 'over the next week.' A regional source later told CNN that talks appeared back on track hours after Iran's suspension. Brent crude oil futures fell to approximately $91-96/bbl on signs of potential resumption.

media.caption: Iran formally suspends ceasefire talks with US; IRGC threatens to close Bab el-Mandeb Strait — Day 94 of US-Iran war

title: Hegseth Blocks 7 Navy Captain-to-Admiral Promotions — Including Women and Black Officers; Fast-Tracks Personal Aide
detail: Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth personally blocked at least 7 officers from a list of 22 Navy captain-to-one-star-admiral promotions, with reporting confirming at least 2 women and 2 Black men were among those removed. Hegseth simultaneously attempted to fast-track a personal aide who had been passed over for promotion multiple times. Senator Jack Reed (D-RI), ranking member of the Armed Services Committee, noted that nearly 60% of senior officers Hegseth has fired or blocked overall are female or Black, citing a pattern of discriminatory promotion practices. The move came alongside a DC Circuit Court of Appeals ruling (June 1) finding his transgender military service ban was 'fueled by the bare desire to harm a politically unpopular group' and likely violates equal protection guarantees. Hegseth posted 'See you at SCOTUS' in response to the transgender ban ruling, signaling a Supreme Court appeal.

media.caption: Hegseth blocks 7 Navy captain-to-admiral promotions including women and Black officers

title: Midterm Primaries in 6 States — Trump Endorses Hilton for California Governor; Rubio, Mullin, Blanche Testify on Capitol Hill
detail: On June 2, 2026, midterm primary elections were held in six states: California, Iowa, Montana, New Jersey, New Mexico, and South Dakota. Trump publicly urged California voters to support his endorsed candidate Steve Hilton — a former adviser to UK Prime Minister David Cameron turned Fox News host — in the California Republican gubernatorial primary. Separately, Secretary of State Marco Rubio testified before congressional committees on his department's budget amid ongoing Iran war deliberations. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin and acting AG Todd Blanche appeared in separate hearings. The primaries continued the season where Trump had already notched MAGA primary victories: defeating Sen. Bill Cassidy in Louisiana (May 16) and Rep. Thomas Massie in Kentucky (May 19-20).

media.caption: Midterm primaries held in six states on June 2, 2026; Trump endorses Steve Hilton for California governor
